Let \( g \) be the number of gold coins and \( s \) be the number of silver coins.  
We know:  
\( g + s = 110 \)  
\( g = s + 30 \)  

Substitute \( s + 30 \) for \( g \) in the first equation:  
\( (s + 30) + s = 110 \)  
\( 2s + 30 = 110 \)  
\( 2s = 80 \)  
\( s = 40 \)  

Then \( g = 40 + 30 = 70 \).  

Answer: 70
reasoning: We are given: "Gretchen has 110 coins. There are 30 more gold coins than silver coins. How many gold coins does Gretchen have?" So we need to set up an equation. Let G = number of gold coins, S = number of silver coins. Then G + S = 110. Also G = S + 30. Substitute: (S+30) + S = 110 => 2S + 30 = 110 => 2S = 80 => S = 40. Then G = 40 + 30 = 70. So gold coins = 70. Answer: 70.
